title: Question 12

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Show that the energy equivalent to a mass of 1.00 u is 934 MeV.

markscheme_points.text: or binding energy = 8.443 × 95 [or equivalent using La-139 nucleus]

hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in nuclear physics and radioactive decay connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Nuclear physics and radioactive decay. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
E = (3.0 × 108)2 × 1.66 × 10-27 (= 1.49 × 10-10 J); E = (1.49 × 10-10) / (1.60 × 10-19) = 9.34 × 108 = 934 MeV; or binding energy = 8.443 × 95 [or equivalent using La-139 nucleus]; binding energy / mass defect = (8.443 × 95) / 0.859 = 934 MeV
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Calculate the total energy, in MeV, released in this nuclear reaction.
$energy = MeV $
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in A Level Physics theory and principles connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: A level physics theory and principles. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
energy = {(1.219 + 0.859) - 1.865)} × 934 or energy = (95 × 8.443) + (139 × 8.189) - (235 × 7.412); = 199 MeV
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The nuclei in $1.2 \times 10^{-7}\,\mathrm{mol}$ of uranium-235 all undergo this reaction in a time of 25 ms.
Calculate the average power release during the time of 25 ms.
$power = W $
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in A Level Physics theory and principles connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: A level physics theory and principles. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
number of reactions = 1.2 × 10-7 × 6.02 × 1023 = 7.22 × 1016; energy release (for one reaction) = 199 × 1.60 × 10-13 (= 3.18 × 10-11 J); power = (7.22 × 1016 × 3.18 × 10-11) / (25 × 10-3) = 9.2 × 107 W
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.
